rubric.statement: The proof inspects `prediction.trajectory['observation_0']`, because synchronous `ReAct.forward` writes each tool outcome there and converts tool exceptions into observation text instead of raising them from the agent call.

The same synchronous `dspy.ReAct` agent with the same async tool is run twice under `dspy.context`, once with `allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=False` and once with it set to `True`, since the conversion flag is checked inside `Tool.__call__` at execution time.
In the disabled-conversion run, the first tool observation is validated as an async-to-sync failure string containing `allow_tool_async_sync_conversion` (and/or `acall`), not as a normal tool value.
In the enabled-conversion run, the first tool observation is asserted to equal the real async tool return value exactly, proving the coroutine result is surfaced through the synchronous workflow.
The scripted agent run forces an actual tool step before selecting `finish`, so `observation_0` exists in both runs and the program can terminate after recording that observation.
